technique: repetition with a difference — a word or shape returning changed
lesson: Today we work on one technique. It is repetition with a difference. That means a word comes back, but something around it has changed. This poem does it with the word "holding." First you get "the house holding its own cold around your sleep." That is the house doing it while you lie still. Then you get "bare trees holding their posts against the hard of the season." Same word, but now it is outdoors, and it means standing firm against the weather. The repeat makes you connect the two moments. The house kept the cold in, and now the trees take the cold on. You feel the poem move you from bed to the open air. Try this: pick one plain verb and use it twice, and change what it is doing the second time. The second time through, listen for the word "holding" coming back. Here is the poem.
poem:
Breath first—the slow pull of it, chest lifting
under the weight of blankets gone heavy with you,
and the house holding its own cold around your sleep.
Your feet find the floor the way a thing finds its level,
sure of the planks, the grain worn smooth to your soles.
Somewhere a board waits to be measured twice,
a line to be drawn clean and cut to its number—
work for the hands that like a close and honest fit.
The window's gone pale now, the hills laid out gray and plain,
bare trees holding their posts against the hard of the season.
You stand, and the day stands with you, square and willing.

The cold air's already outside, waiting—
pull on your boots and go meet it.
